repeat_scope: Second independent sample of the same nine High-profile scenarios at identical arguments, run with stall attribution instrumentation. This does not supersede the first capture; both are samples of the same configuration and the difference between them is the finding.
headline: Second sample of the nine High-profile scenarios at identical arguments, with stall attribution instrumentation active. Zero steady-driving stalls were recorded, against twelve eleven hours earlier on the same machine at the same content. Every evaluated threshold passes, including the zero-stall limit that failed in four scenarios before. The instrumentation captured no attribution data because there was nothing to attribute. The finding is that the failure is not reproducible; that is consistent with a machine-state, contention, or measurement-method cause but excludes no candidate, including an intermittent content, code, driver, or instrumentation cause, which need not appear in any given matrix. One run, streaming-repeat-2, recorded mean render GPU time about ten times its siblings without any stall.

streaming_repeatability.purpose: Characterise the single 52.404 ms steady-driving stall recorded in the merged balanced baseline (Q-022a working default A).
streaming_repeatability.statistical_claim: Three runs establish a repeat count, not a confidence interval. No rate is claimed beyond the observed counts.

stall_characterisation.attribution: Every recorded stall reports render CPU plus render GPU far below the stall duration, so the cost is outside the measured render components. The harness has no per-subsystem counter, so no more specific cause is claimed here; Q-022c owns how attribution should be obtained.

human_gate.name: Q-022 owner ratification of derived subsystem and content-class budgets

identical: route package inputs and their hashes
differed: the repeat build carries the stall attribution instrumentation; a before/after comparison showed it allocation-neutral, but its timing cost was never separately measured, so it is not excluded as a variable
reproducibility_finding.interpretation: Twelve steady-driving stalls became zero with no change to content, arguments, or inputs. This is consistent with a machine-state, contention, or measurement-method cause. It does not establish one, and it excludes none: an intermittent content, code, or driver cause is precisely the kind that need not appear in any given matrix, so non-reproduction is not evidence against it. The first capture's events were real measurements and are not withdrawn.
reproducibility_finding.consequence_for_the_threshold: The zero-stall limit is a binary gate on a rare event that this evidence shows is sensitive to conditions outside the build. Whether it should be gated that way is Q-022a.

external_timing_anomaly.observation: This run's whole distribution shifted, without producing any stall.
external_timing_anomaly.reading: Mean render GPU time was roughly ten times its sibling runs at identical arguments while frame rate fell by a similar factor. The harness cannot say why: contention from another GPU client, thermal or power state, a driver-side event, and compositor behaviour are all candidates and nothing recorded distinguishes them. What it shows is that a capture's GPU timing can change by an order of magnitude between otherwise identical runs without the build changing, on a metric the workspace policy does not observe.
external_timing_anomaly.handling: Reported, not discarded. Excluding it would improve every summary number and hide the measurement-method problem it demonstrates.
